title: Platform - Storage
description: Node disk space and I/O, Kubernetes volume claims and application self-reported storage. openebs-hostpath volumes share the node filesystem, which is authoritative for free space.

panels.title: Node filesystem space used
panels.description: Used share of each real node filesystem (tmpfs, overlay, squashfs and /run excluded); every hostpath volume consumes this space. NodeFilesystemLowSpace fires above 85% used for 10 minutes.

panels.title: Node filesystem available / size
panels.description: Free and total bytes per node filesystem. Authoritative for free space because every openebs-hostpath volume shares it; find the growing consumer in the rows below.

panels.title: Days until full at the 24h trend (absent = not filling)
panels.description: Available bytes divided by the 24h least-squares decline rate; only shrinking filesystems appear. Short write bursts (image pulls, restores, compaction) make it look worse than it is.

panels.title: Projected available space in 3 days (6h linear trend, same as alert; below 0 = full)
panels.description: Free space predicted 3 days ahead from the 6h trend, the same expression as NodeFilesystemFillingUp; below 0 means full. Short bursts exaggerate it, so confirm the trend before deleting data.

panels.title: Node filesystem inodes used
panels.description: Used share of inodes per real node filesystem. Running out blocks writes even with free bytes; look for directories with many small files.

panels.title: Disk throughput: read / write
panels.description: Bytes read and written per second per whole block device (loop and RAM devices excluded). Read it with latency to tell heavy but healthy from struggling.

panels.title: Disk IOPS: completed reads / writes
panels.description: Completed reads and writes per second per block device. With throughput, it shows whether load is many small or few large I/Os.

panels.title: Average latency per completed read / write
panels.description: Average time per completed read and write. Gaps mean nothing completed, not zero latency; rising latency with queue depth means the disk is saturated.

panels.title: Disk busy time (utilisation)
panels.description: Share of wall time with at least one I/O in flight. NVMe serves many requests in parallel, so 100% busy is not necessarily saturated; compare with queue depth and latency.

panels.title: Average I/O queue depth (saturation)
panels.description: Average number of I/O requests in flight. Sustained values well above 1 with rising latency mean the disk cannot keep up.

panels.title: PVC inventory: requested size, storage class and bound volume
panels.description: Requested size is a scheduling hint only for openebs-hostpath; nothing stops a volume from growing past it.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (kube_persistentvolumeclaim_resource_requests_storage_bytes) * on (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left (storageclass, volumename) max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim, storageclass, volumename) (kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info)

panels.title: PVCs without kubelet volume stats (empty = all reported)
panels.description: Claims known to kube-state-metrics that kubelet does not report. Their used/available panels below stay empty; that is unknown, not an empty volume.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim, storageclass) (kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info) unless on (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes

panels.title: Kubelet volume used / capacity
panels.description: For openebs-hostpath both lines may equal the whole node filesystem rather than this volume.

panels.title: Kubelet volume available
panels.description: For openebs-hostpath this may be the node filesystem free space, shared by every volume.

panels.title: Kubelet volume used % of reported capacity
panels.description: Percent of kubelet-reported capacity, not of the requested PVC size. Identical lines across PVCs mean filesystem-wide reporting.

targets.expr: 100 * max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes) / max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes)

panels.title: Kubelet volume used growth / 1 hour
panels.description: Change of kubelet used bytes over the previous hour; negative means space was freed. Filesystem-wide reporting makes every PVC show the same node-level growth.

panels.title: Kubelet volume used growth / 24 hours
panels.description: Change of kubelet used bytes over the previous 24 hours; negative means space was freed. Needs 24h of retained history.

panels.title: Prometheus TSDB on-disk size vs size cap
panels.description: Blocks, WAL and memory-mapped head chunks together approximate the Prometheus volume usage. The size cap is retentionSize; 0 would mean disabled.

panels.title: Prometheus head series
panels.description: Active series in memory; sustained growth drives both memory and block size.

panels.title: Prometheus retention block deletions / 24 hours: size vs time
panels.description: Size-triggered deletions mean the 8GB cap, not the 7d retention, is limiting history.

panels.title: AnkiLabs PostgreSQL database size
panels.description: pg_database_size per database from the ankilabs postgres-exporter. Excludes WAL; compare with the node filesystem for total impact.

panels.title: OpenEBS hostpath provisioner logs only
panels.description: Volume create/delete activity and provisioning failures. A pending PVC with no matching record here points at scheduling or storage-class selection instead.
